scope: Active Next.js API and browser workflows, authentication, authorization, evidence, banking, dashboards, and events
Go insurance chaincode: policy, claim, invoice, Oracle, review, evidence, settlement, partner, banking, and benefit boundaries
Oracle worker protocol, persistence, startup, and reconnect behavior
Network/release scripts, CI checks, executable workflow model, and research/security regression tests

findings.description: Restricted policy statement exports to owning policyholders, insurers, and auditors.
Scoped subjectless policyholder notifications to ledger-owned claims and policies; fail closed when ownership cannot be checked.
Rejected inherited object properties as demo accounts and malformed session-token suffixes.
Unified API/workflow IDs with Go's 3–128-character key format and rejected impossible calendar dates.
Invalidated OTP challenges when the selected policy or source account changes; report failed sign-out requests.
Invalidated ciphertext when claim/evidence bindings change and disabled binding edits during encryption/upload.
Prevented one premium from buying a period longer than its configured interval.
Required the premium destination account to belong to the insurer.
Enforced mandate period expiry and rejected mandate expiry before its next debit.
Rejected negative/overflowed bank balances and overflow in premium reversal limits.
Kept the final coverage date inclusive and allowed unpaid policies to expire.
Aligned issued-policy paid-through and next-due dates, including coverage shorter than one interval.
Enforced agreement effective/expiry dates using the Fabric transaction timestamp.
Derived payment communications from the final event actually committed by Fabric.
Serialized registry publication within the web process and reused unchanged snapshots.
Discarded a transaction checkpoint when advancing the configured start block; rejected invalid persisted block numbers.
Attached the stream consumer before asynchronous health-file work could expose an unhandled gRPC stream error.
Loaded only dashboard collections used by each role.
Removed an unreachable premium-receipt helper and duplicate ignore rules.
Added formal-model and research/security regression checks to CI and the local verifier; made Go verification check formatting without rewriting source.
Detected newly added runtime source files omitted from a chaincode package.
Added browser/API checks that can run without Fabric/Oracle services or ledger writes.
Updated sharp to 0.35.5 and source-map-js to 1.2.2 within existing constraints.
Updated Go gRPC to 1.83.2 and compatible transitive libraries while retaining Go 1.25. The rescan no longer reports gRPC findings; Go standard-library and x/net HTTP/2 findings remain.

oracleWorkerUnavailablePeerRecovery.observation: Worker remained alive, persisted DEGRADED health, and retried the stopped peer at least twice using an isolated state root and health port.

coverage: Invalid state keys and calendar dates

liveFabricJourneys.reason: Fabric network containers were stopped. The audit did not start, reset, redeploy, or write to a preserved Fabric channel.

webFullAudit.reason: No patched braces release was listed by the advisory. npm's proposed alternative was an incompatible major downgrade of eslint-config-next; the full audit gate was retained.

goVulnerabilityScan.interpretation: Static call reachability does not establish exploitability in the configured Fabric deployment.

followups.action: Upgrade the Fabric chaincode build/test toolchain together with its deployment builder to a supported patched Go release (at least Go 1.26.9 for the recorded standard-library findings), then upgrade x/net to at least 0.60.0 and rerun govulncheck and the live Fabric gate.
followups.reason: The x/net 0.60.0 patch requires Go 1.26.0. The current source/build scripts deliberately retain the project's Go 1.25 baseline.

followups.action: Update the development ESLint dependency chain when an upstream fix becomes available. The existing full npm audit remains non-green until this is resolved.
Package/deploy the changed chaincode to an isolated verification channel and run the full live workflow suite before using the fixes on a preserved demonstration channel.
followups.reason: Source tests and offline browser checks passed; these are not a live Fabric compatibility result.

limitations: Registry publication serialization is scoped to the existing web process; multiple web replicas would require shared concurrency control.
Archived benchmark measurements were preserved and are not measurements of this modified source tree.
